rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi recalls the Prophet calling him his trusted one; after Ali's accession he sold his property and followed Ali through Basra, Ṣiffīn, and Nahrawān.
rows.anchor: إن لكل نبي أمينا، وإن أميني أبو رافع

rows.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
rows.claim: Ammar reports that Ali gave a ring to a petitioner while bowing in a voluntary prayer; the verse descended, and the Prophet proclaimed Ali his mawla.
rows.anchor: سمعت عمار بن ياسر يقول وقف لعلي بن أبي طالب سائل وهو راكع في صلاة تطوع

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: One of the two Imams reports that the revelation of this verse distressed the Prophet, who feared Quraysh would deny him; God then commanded him in 5:67 to proclaim it at Ghadir Khumm.
rows.anchor: عن المفضل بن صالح، عن بعض أصحابه، عن أحدهما عليهما السلام

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: One of the two Imams reports that God instructed the Prophet to love Ali, Abu Dharr, Salman, and Miqdad; only three people knew the matter of authority.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جميلة عن بعض أصحابه عن أحدهما عليهما السلام قال إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم قال

rows.speaker: أحدهما عليهما السلام
rows.claim: The report concludes that people who came to the knowledgeable authorities did not ask whom the verses on authority referred to.
rows.anchor: من ثم أتاهم لم يكونوا يسألون

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: In his appeal to Abu Bakr, Ali asks whether God's authority joined to the Messenger's in the ring-alms verse belonged to him or Abu Bakr; Abu Bakr answers that it belonged to Ali.
rows.anchor: في حديث مناشدة علي عليه السلام لأبي بكر حين ولي أبو بكر الخلافة، وذكر عليه السلام فضائله

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr reports Ali's challenge at the shura: no one else gave alms while bowing and had this verse revealed about him; the other candidates agreed.
rows.anchor: إلى أبي ذر في حديث مناشدة أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام عثمان والزبير وعبد الرحمن بن عوف وسعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: علي بن محمد الهادي
rows.claim: Al-Hadi's letter treats the Qur'an and the community's agreement on its truth as decisive evidence, interpreting the hadith about communal consensus as excluding fabricated reports and readings that overturn clear scripture.
rows.anchor: علي بن محمد الهادي عليه السلام إلى أهل الأهواز حين سألوه عن الجبر والتفويض. قال عليه السلام اجتمعت الأمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author cites the Thaqalayn reports that the Qur'an and the Prophet's family will not part, and says verse 5:55 is a scriptural witness to that hadith.
rows.anchor: وجدنا شواهد هذا الحديث نصا في كتاب الله مثل قوله { إنما وليكم الله ورسوله والذين آمنوا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says scholars' reports agree that Ali gave his ring while bowing, for which God praised him and revealed the verse.
rows.anchor: ثم اتفقت روايات العلماء في ذلك لأمير المؤمنين عليه السلام أنه تصدق بخاتمه وهو راكع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author adduces the Prophet's declarations naming Ali as mawla, successor who settles debts and fulfills promises, and deputy like Aaron to Moses except for prophethood.
rows.anchor: قد أبانه من أصحابه بهذه اللفظة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because the Qur'an confirms these reports and they in turn clarify the Qur'an, the author says the community must acknowledge them; only obstinacy and corruption lead to refusal.
rows.anchor: فعلمنا أن الكتاب شهد بتصديق هذه الأخبار، وتحقيق هذه الشواهد

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali reports that hypocrites asked whether any further duty remained; God identified wilayah as the single admonition in 34:46 and revealed 5:55, with only one man giving alms while bowing.
rows.anchor: وفي الاحتجاج في حديث عن أمير المؤمنين عليه السلام قال المنافقون لرسول الله صلى الله عليه وآله وسلم هل بقي لربك علينا

rows.speaker: أبو عبد الله عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Sadiq answers that obedience to the successors is obligatory and identifies them as those described in 4:59 and 5:55.
rows.anchor: قلت لأبي عبد الله عليه السلام الأوصياء طاعتهم مفترضة؟ فقال نعم، هم الذين قال الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author explains that attributing revelation about Ali to all the Imams reflects their single household and unified affair.
rows.anchor: وإسناد نزول ما نزل في علي عليه السلام إلى جميع الأئمة عليهم السلام لكونهم أهل بيت واحد، وأمرهم واحد.

rows.speaker: أبو ذر
rows.claim: Abu Dharr recounts Ali giving a ring to a petitioner while bowing, then the Prophet praying that Ali be his minister as Aaron was to Moses; Gabriel brought 5:55 in response, and Abu Dharr calls Ali leader of the righteous and slayer of unbelievers.
rows.anchor: فكشف العمامة عن وجهه وقال يا أيها الناس من عرفني فقد عرفني ومن لم يعرفني فأنا جندب بن جنادة البدري أبو ذر الغفاري

rows.speaker: ابن سلام
rows.claim: Ibn Salam reports that converts ostracized by their people witnessed Ali give his ring while bowing; the Prophet recited both verses after learning of the gift.
rows.anchor: من صحيح النسائي عن ابن سلام قال أتيت رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم فقلنا إن قومنا حادونا لما صدقنا الله ورسوله

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reports from Ibn Abbas that 5:55 was revealed about Ali.
rows.anchor: أخبرنا مجاهد عن ابن عباس في قوله تعالى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ali gave his ring to a poor man while bowing, after which the Prophet asked who had given it and the verse descended.
rows.anchor: عن أبي صالح، عن ابن عباس قال كان علي راكعا فجاءه مسكين

rows.speaker: أبو جعفر عليه السلام
rows.claim: Al-Baqir identifies Ali, rather than Ibn Salam, as the one possessing knowledge of the Book and as the witness in 13:43 and 11:17; he says verses including 5:55 were revealed about Ali.
rows.anchor: عن أبي جعفر، قال كنت عند أبي جعفر جالسا إذ مر عليه ابن عبد الله بن سلام

rows.speaker: عمرو بن العاص
rows.claim: Amr tells Muawiya that several verses of distinctive merit were revealed for Ali, including 5:55, alongside verses about vows, the witness, fidelity, and affection for kin.
rows.anchor: في جواب مكاتبة معاوية إلى عمرو بن العاص قال عمرو بن العاص لقد علمت يا معاوية ما أنزل في كتابه من الآيات

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas reports that Ibn Salam and fellow converts complained that their community shunned them and the Prophet answered by reciting 5:55.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس قال أقبل عبد الله بن سلام ومعه نفر من قومه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: In Ibn Abbas's report, the petitioner identifies Ali as the ring-giver and says he gave it while bowing; the Prophet then recites 5:56, completing the response to Ibn Salam's group's complaint.
rows.anchor: خرج إلى المسجد والناس بين قائم وراكع، وبصر بسائل

rows.speaker: حسان بن ثابت
rows.claim: Hassan ibn Thabit's poem praises Ali for giving his blessed ring while bowing and says God revealed the best authority for him in definitive ordinances.
rows.anchor: فأنشأ حسان بن ثابت يقول أبا حسن تفديك نفسي ومهجتي وكل بطيء في الهدى ومسارع

rows.speaker: أنس بن مالك
rows.claim: Anas reports that Ali gestured for a petitioner to take his ring while he bowed; the Prophet told Umar Paradise was assured for Ali, who thereby shed every sin and error.
rows.anchor: أن سائلا أتى المسجد وهو يقول من يقرض الملي الوفي؟ وعلي راكع يقول بيده خلفه للسائل

rows.speaker: عمار بن ياسر
rows.claim: Ammar reports that Ali gave a ring to a petitioner during a voluntary prayer, prompting the verse's revelation and the Prophet's declaration that Ali was his mawla.
rows.anchor: عن أبيه، عن جده قال سمعت عمار بن ياسر - رضي الله عنه - يقول وقف لعلي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: جابر
rows.claim: Jabir reports that Ibn Salam and companions complained of social isolation; a petitioner then said Ali gave him a ring while bowing, and the verse was revealed.
rows.anchor: عن أبي الزبير، عن جابر - رضي الله عنه - قال جاء عبد الله بن سلام

rows.speaker: سلمة بن كهيل
rows.claim: Salama ibn Kuhayl reports that Ali gave his ring while bowing and the verse descended.
rows.anchor: عن موسى بن قيس الحضرمي عن سلمة بن كهيل قال تصدق علي بخاتمه وهو راكع فنزلت

rows.speaker: أبو رافع
rows.claim: Abu Rafi says the Prophet recited the verse while waking from revelation; he later foretold that people would fight Ali and prescribed resistance by hand, tongue, or heart according to ability.
rows.anchor: يا أبا رافع سيكون بعدي قوم يقاتلون عليا حق على الله جهادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says reports of the ring-giving occasion are numerous and available in their cited books; he selected several accounts because their wording of the episode varies.
rows.anchor: أقول والروايات في نزول الآيتين في قصة التصدق بالخاتم كثيرة أخرجنا عدة منها من كتاب غاية المرام للبحراني

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says Companions and Imams widely transmitted the episode, and major tafsir and hadith authorities including Ahmad, al-Nasa'i, al-Tabari, and al-Tabarani accepted it without refutation; theologians also acknowledged its report.
rows.anchor: وقد اتفق على نقلها من غير رد أئمة التفسير المأثور كأحمد والنسائي والطبري والطبراني وعبد بن حميد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists cite the report when discussing extensive movement during prayer and whether voluntary almsgiving counts as zakat.
rows.anchor: وأوردها الفقهاء في مسألة الفعل الكثير من بحث الصلاة، وفي مسألة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Leading literary commentators such as al-Zamakhshari and Abu Hayyan did not question that the verse applies to the ring-giving report, nor did language authorities challenge the report's wording.
rows.anchor: ولم يناقش في صحة انطباق الآية على الرواية فحول الأدب من المفسرين كالزمخشري في الكشاف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects claims that the ring report was fabricated, especially Ibn Taymiyya's assertion of scholarly consensus that it was forged, calling that claim extraordinary.
rows.anchor: فلا يعبأ بما ذكره بعضهم أن حديث نزول الآية في قصة الخاتم موضوع مختلق، وقد أفرط بعضهم كشيخ الإسلام ابن تيمية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author sees 23:9's wording, echoing 23:2, as supporting inward humility and awe as the sense of guarding prayer here, though the familiar exegesis takes it as keeping prayer times.
rows.anchor: المؤمنون 19، كما بدأ بمعناها في أولها فقال الذين هم في صلاتهم خاشعون المؤمنون 2. وهذا هو الذي يؤيد

rows.speaker: الراغب
rows.claim: Al-Raghib traces baraka from the camel's breast and kneeling, hence steadfastness; in Qur'anic usage it is settled divine good, including imperceptible increase, so the charity saying means no loss of true blessing rather than no measurable decrease. Tabāraka denotes God's exclusive possession of good.
rows.anchor: ذكر الراغب في المفردات أن أصل البرك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Blessing is stable good relative to an aim: Abraham's household receives spiritual and material goods, while food's blessing may mean nourishment, safety, healing, or inward strength for worship; God fixes such good by arranging causes and removing impediments.
rows.anchor: رحمة الله وبركاته عليكم أهل البيت هود 73 خيرات متنوعة معنوية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Death and life are divine acts with angels as their causes; the soul is a nonmaterial kind of existence that unites with and relates to the body in a nonmaterial way.
rows.anchor: وأنه هو أمات وأحيا النجم 44 فالأمر تكويني والملائكة من أسبابه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command to bring out the souls is an implicit and imaginative metaphor, picturing the soul as within the body and death as its departure; it means severing the soul's attachment to the body.
rows.anchor: فالمراد بقوله { أخرجوا أنفسكم } قطع علقه أنفسهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The angels address the wrongdoers during death's agonies, violently seizing their souls and announcing humiliating punishment in the world of death for lying about God and rejecting His signs arrogantly.
rows.anchor: والملائكة آخذون في تعذيبهم بالقبض الشديد العنيف لأرواحهم وإنبائهم بأنهم واقعون في عالم الموت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Farādā means individuals detached from others, contrasted with a pair and conceptually close to odd versus even.
rows.anchor: الفرادى جمع فرد وهو الذي انفصل عن اختلاط غيره نوعا من الاختلاط

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Takhwīl means giving assets or similar resources that a person manages and disposes of.
rows.anchor: والتخويل إعطاء الخول أي المال ونحوه الذي يقوم الإنسان به بالتدبير والتصرف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The alleged intercessors are deities worshipped apart from God to intercede with Him, thereby treated as partners in His creation.
rows.anchor: والمراد بالشفعاء الأرباب المعبودون من دون الله ليكونوا شفعاء عند الله فعادوا بذلك شركاء لله سبحانه في خلقه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: At return to God after death, people appear alone as at their first creation and recognize that God alone governed them; wealth, family, social backing, and alleged intercessors were false claims without real creative power.
rows.anchor: والآية تنبئ عن حقيقة الحياة الإنسانية التي ستظهر له حينما يقدم على ربه بالتوفي فيشاهد حقيقة أمر نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Human beings and all other things remain under God's governance and goal; apparent causes are only means whose effects end in God and possess no independent efficacy, though worldly desire makes people treat them as autonomous.
rows.anchor: فالإنسان جزء من أجزاء الكون واقع تحت التدبير الإلهي متوجه إلى الغاية التي غياها الله سبحانه له كسائر أجزاء الكون
